text:
[LCRS.17.1] **Success is silence.** A call to a service that declares
`no response` ([LADP.8.4.2]) asserts nothing when it succeeds: no
response fact exists for it, so none is retained ([LCRS.6.6.1]). When it
fails, the adapter asserts a `CallError` ([LCRS.4.2.1]) as for any call. An
adapter that learns of the failure only after the call has returned asserts the
`CallError` then.

Silence is never mistaken for a timeout: the engine tracks no pending call
([LCRS.10.6.1]), and a timeout is a continuation or an absence pattern the
author writes ([LCRS.7.1]).

idris.name: lcrs_17_1__no_response_sweeps_error_alone
idris.note: A `no response` service's call sweeps CallError alone: a transcription, said so.

idris.name: lcrs_17_1__no_response_sweeps_error_only
idris.note: The `no response` call's sweep of CallError alone, computed. LESS than the clause: the adapter's failure path is the host's assert.

idris.name: lcrs_6_2_1__site_ping
idris.note: A fixture. Success is silence: the host asserts the CallError of the witness; the adapter is not modelled.

idris.name: lcrs_6_2_1__swept_by_call
idris.note: The kinds a call sweeps: the site's response schema and CallError, or CallError alone for a `no response` service.

tla.name: lcrs_17_1__silent
tla.note: Whether a call is to a `no response` service, fixed at Init and explored both ways. Success is silence, which is no step of the model; failure asserts a CallError, the one answer such a call can have.

tla.name: lcrs_4_2_2__Respond
tla.note: The adapter's answer to a call of a `no response` service can only be a CallError.

tla.name: lcrs_4_2_2__one_kind_when_live
tla.note: A live answer of a `no response` service is a CallError, at every reachable state. Bounded: two calls, every assignment of `no response`.
